note: Use of English reading text: The Lekki Headmaster (Kabir Alabi Garba), the UTME recommended novel. 10 appear in every JAMB mock.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: The Lekki Headmaster was written by
questions.A: Kabir Alabi Garba
questions.B: Khadija Abubakar Jalli
questions.C: Abimbola Adelakun
questions.D: Chinua Achebe
questions.explanation: Kabir Alabi Garba, a journalist, wrote The Lekki Headmaster; Khadija Jalli wrote the earlier UTME text The Life Changer.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the main setting of the story is
questions.A: a public school in Ibadan
questions.B: the passport office in Agodi
questions.C: a college in Manchester
questions.D: Stardom Schools in Lekki, Lagos
questions.explanation: The action centres on Stardom Schools, the elite private school in Lekki, Lagos, where Bepo is principal.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the titles of the first and last chapters, 'Dusk' and '...Dawn', suggest
questions.A: the passing of a single school day
questions.B: the school's morning and evening prayers
questions.C: the harmattan season in Lagos
questions.D: a movement from despair to renewed hope
questions.explanation: The novel opens in gloom with Bepo's breakdown ('Dusk') and closes with his joyful return ('Dawn'): darkness giving way to light.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo lives in
questions.A: the staff quarters in Lekki
questions.B: Badagry
questions.C: Ibadan, Oyo State
questions.D: Ikeja, Lagos
questions.explanation: Bepo's home is in Ikeja; he leaves from there for the airport and receives Mrs Ignatius's late-night call there.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: The expression 'japa syndrome', as used in The Lekki Headmaster, refers to
questions.A: a tropical illness common in Lagos
questions.B: a rule against lateness at Stardom
questions.C: a traditional dance from Badagry
questions.D: the mass rush of Nigerians to relocate abroad
questions.explanation: 'Japa' is Nigerian slang for fleeing the country; the novel treats the migration wave as a national obsession.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the author uses flashbacks mainly to
questions.A: describe Bepo's childhood and secondary school days in Ikeja
questions.B: explain how Chief David Aje built Stardom Schools from nothing
questions.C: reveal Bepo's earlier experiences at Beesway and Fruitful Future
questions.D: narrate Seri's early struggles as a nurse in London
questions.explanation: Bepo's memories of Beesway Group of School, Fruitful Future and his poor early years are told as flashbacks.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the novel opens with Bepo
questions.A: receiving a late-night call from a parent
questions.B: boarding an evening flight to London
questions.C: renewing his passport in Ibadan
questions.D: breaking down in tears at the morning assembly
questions.explanation: In the opening chapter, 'Dusk', the normally lively principal weeps uncontrollably before the whole school at assembly.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, when Bepo breaks down at the assembly, the person who takes charge is
questions.A: Mrs Ibidun Gloss, the Managing Director
questions.B: Mr Audu, the Fine Arts teacher
questions.C: Mrs Grace Apeh, the Vice Principal
questions.D: Mr Ope Wande, the Physics teacher
questions.explanation: The Vice Principal, Mrs Grace Apeh, ends the assembly and leads Bepo to his office before calling the MD.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Mr Ope Wande, who is asked to speak with the weeping principal, is
questions.A: the school nurse and a deacon
questions.B: the guidance counsellor
questions.C: a Physics teacher and a pastor
questions.D: a lawyer on the school board
questions.explanation: The MD calls in Mr Wande because, besides teaching Physics, he is a pastor who could counsel Bepo.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the MD sends the weeping Bepo home because she reasons that the school is
questions.A: a family that must protect its own members from public shame
questions.B: in danger of losing its licence if the inspectors see him
questions.C: closing early that day for the mid-term holiday in any case
questions.D: not a rehabilitation centre but a place for learning and earning money
questions.explanation: Mrs Gloss puts the school's image and business first, saying it is 'not a rehabilitation centre'.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the day before Bepo's breakdown, the school had celebrated
questions.A: a 90 per cent success rate in the WASSCE
questions.B: the opening of a new boarding house
questions.C: Bepo's twenty-fourth anniversary
questions.D: victory in a football competition
questions.explanation: Top-performing teachers had just received cash prizes for the school's 90 per cent WASSCE success, which makes the breakdown more shocking.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Stardom's management reduced boarding fees from N250,000 to N165,000 in order to
questions.A: help parents who had been badly hit by the economic recession
questions.B: compete with the cheaper fees charged by Beesway Group of School
questions.C: move more pupils into the boarding house and reduce lateness
questions.D: obey a new directive from the Lagos State Ministry of Education
questions.explanation: The fee cut moved 80 per cent of pupils into boarding and cut lateness, while the excursion fee was quietly raised.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Ikenna Egbu's speech about the excursion to Jos is significant because he
questions.A: announces that Bepo is leaving the school
questions.B: wins the prize for best speaker
questions.C: complains about the new school fees
questions.D: praises Nigeria and rejects the idea of migrating abroad
questions.explanation: The SSS 1 boy says he would rather settle in Jos than 'japa' to Canada or London, a patriotic note that contrasts with Bepo's crisis.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo's cry of 'Oluwa gba mi o!' during his breakdown means
questions.A: 'Leave me alone!'
questions.B: 'I am going home!'
questions.C: 'God, save me!'
questions.D: 'Forgive me, my people!'
questions.explanation: The Yoruba exclamation 'Oluwa gba mi o' means 'God, save me', showing the depth of Bepo's distress.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the real reason for Bepo's distress is that he
questions.A: has been sacked by the Managing Director
questions.B: has been accused of a grammatical error
questions.C: has lost his savings in the cooperative
questions.D: has finally agreed to relocate to the United Kingdom
questions.explanation: After five days Bepo reveals that he is leaving Stardom to join his family in the UK, a decision he hates.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo's wife, Seri, works in the United Kingdom as
questions.A: a secondary school teacher
questions.B: a hairdresser
questions.C: a nurse
questions.D: an accountant
questions.explanation: Seri is a nurse in the UK, rumoured by the staff to earn up to 10,000 pounds a month.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo's two daughters are
questions.A: Nike and Kike
questions.B: Bibi and Kemi
questions.C: Favour and Nike
questions.D: Kemi and Favour
questions.explanation: Nike and Kike live with their mother Seri in the UK; Bibi, Kemi and Favour are other children in the story.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo earned the nickname 'The Lekki Headmaster' because he
questions.A: was the oldest and longest-serving principal in the whole of Lekki
questions.B: came from a long line of headmasters in his family in Ikeja
questions.C: founded the first private secondary school on the Lekki peninsula
questions.D: settled staff quarrels like King Oloja of the TV drama Village Headmaster
questions.explanation: Mr Audu likened Bepo's wise handling of staff disputes to King Oloja in Village Headmaster, and the name stuck.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the teacher who coined Bepo's famous nickname is
questions.A: Mr Fafore, the English teacher
questions.B: Mr Wande, the Physics teacher
questions.C: Mr Audu, the Fine Arts teacher
questions.D: Mr Ayesoro, the Government teacher
questions.explanation: The clownish Fine Arts teacher, Mr Audu, first called Bepo 'The Lekki Headmaster'.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, before becoming principal, Bepo headed the primary arm of the school, called
questions.A: Stardom Hub
questions.B: Fruitful Future
questions.C: Beesway Kiddies
questions.D: Stardom Kiddies
questions.explanation: Bepo was headmaster of Stardom Kiddies, the primary section, for four years before rising to principal.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, according to the staff-room debate, Bepo's promised monthly teaching salary in the UK is
questions.A: 3,600 pounds
questions.B: 10,000 pounds
questions.C: 400,000 naira
questions.D: 1,500 pounds
questions.explanation: The teachers compare the 3,600 pounds Bepo will earn abroad with his 400,000 naira salary at Stardom.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo's monthly salary as principal of Stardom Schools is
questions.D: N1.5 million
questions.explanation: Bepo earns 400,000 naira a month; 175,000 naira is Mr Fafore's salary.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo's colleagues find his reluctance to relocate 'extremely funny' because
questions.A: he has never once travelled by air and is secretly afraid of flying
questions.B: he cannot afford the airfare and is too proud to borrow from them
questions.C: he already has a job and family waiting abroad, which many Nigerians crave
questions.D: he is too old, at fifty-one, to start a new career in a foreign land
questions.explanation: To the staff, Bepo is living the dream thousands are sacrificing everything for, so his hesitation seems foolish.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo had planned to retire at fifty-five in order to
questions.A: become a full-time pastor in his church
questions.B: contest for a seat in the House of Assembly
questions.C: write novels about his years in teaching
questions.D: go into business and create jobs for others
questions.explanation: Now fifty-one, Bepo dreamed of retiring at fifty-five to become an employer of labour through farming or transport.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo was wary of the commercial transport business because
questions.A: local drivers and mechanics could not be trusted
questions.B: fuel prices were rising faster than fares
questions.C: the government had banned commercial buses
questions.D: he had never learnt to drive a vehicle himself
questions.explanation: Bepo shelved the bus-leasing idea after hearing how drivers and mechanics collude to defraud vehicle owners.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Mr Audu swears he would slaughter seven cows if
questions.A: Bepo returns to Stardom
questions.B: the staff win the farewell match
questions.C: he ever obtains a visa to travel abroad
questions.D: Mr Fafore is sacked
questions.explanation: Audu, desperate to leave Nigeria himself, jokes that a visa would make him kill seven cows in celebration.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Mr Nku is remembered as the staff member who
questions.A: sold a school bus to fund his son's education
questions.B: was sacked over a grammatical error
questions.C: ran an unauthorised creche beside the school
questions.D: took a N2 million cooperative loan and vanished abroad
questions.explanation: Nku disappeared abroad with a two-million-naira loan from the Stardom cooperative; a driver was the one who tried to sell a bus.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Sola, whom Bepo consults about life abroad, used to teach
questions.A: Home Economics
questions.B: Physics
questions.C: Fine Arts
questions.D: Government
questions.explanation: Sola, a former Home Economics teacher at Stardom, relocated to Manchester with her husband.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo had once saved Sola from being sacked when she
questions.A: ran an unauthorised creche near the school
questions.B: took a loan she could not repay
questions.C: insulted a wealthy parent
questions.D: missed the Open Day
questions.explanation: Sola was caught running a creche without permission; Bepo's intervention kept her job.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Sola's story about her asthmatic daughter illustrates
questions.A: the efficiency of the UK emergency health system
questions.B: the high cost of living in Britain
questions.C: the difficulty of obtaining a visa
questions.D: the loneliness of migrant mothers
questions.explanation: Two ambulances arrived within five minutes of her call, a contrast with the fragile system at home.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Jare the banker and Hope the accountant are mentioned to show
questions.A: that migrants always prosper
questions.B: the benefits of hourly wages
questions.C: the humbling and painful side of migration
questions.D: how to obtain a UK visa
questions.explanation: Jare broke down caring for an elderly couple and Hope's marriage collapsed abroad, the dark side of japa.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the death of Chief Waliem, a wealthy parent, is recalled to show
questions.A: the dangers of driving on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway at night
questions.B: the greed of school owners who chase fees even from the bereaved
questions.C: the generosity of rich parents towards the school's projects
questions.D: how quickly a family's fortune can collapse without a welfare system
questions.explanation: After Waliem's sudden death his family fell into debt and his children left school, unlike families protected by welfare abroad.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo notes that migrants earning in dollars or pounds often save little because
questions.A: they also pay rent, taxes and bills in the same hard currency
questions.B: they send every kobo home to relatives who keep demanding more
questions.C: they are poorly paid compared with citizens of those countries
questions.D: they gamble their earnings away in the casinos of London
questions.explanation: The novel stresses that high foreign wages are matched by high foreign expenses.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the Ignatius family's visa application fails because
questions.A: their documents were discovered to be forged
questions.B: they could not pay the visa agent
questions.C: a DNA test shows that Favour is not Mr Ignatius's biological child
questions.D: Mr Ignatius had a criminal record
questions.explanation: The embassy's mandatory DNA test exposes a family secret, and the visas are denied.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Mrs Ignatius prepared for life in the UK by learning
questions.A: practical nursing skills
questions.B: bread and cake baking
questions.C: commercial bus driving
questions.D: traditional Yoruba hairdressing
questions.explanation: She learnt suku, kojusoko and onilegogoro styles because such skills fetch good money abroad.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo is irritated by Mrs Ignatius's call because
questions.A: it comes near midnight and oversteps a professional boundary
questions.B: she insults his wife and daughters during the conversation
questions.C: she demands a refund of the fees she paid for the whole term
questions.D: she threatens to drag the school to court over her daughter
questions.explanation: The late-night call about her marital crisis shows how wealthy parents treat the principal as an on-call therapist.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Mr Ayesoro is removed from the classroom because
questions.A: he beat a student severely
questions.B: he made a grammatical error in a note
questions.C: a pupil, Bibi, had nightmares about his tribal marks
questions.D: he refused to attend Open Day
questions.explanation: Bibi's mother complained after her daughter's nightmares, and the school moved Mr Ayesoro out of teaching.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Mr Ayesoro taught
questions.A: English Language
questions.B: Fine Arts
questions.C: Physics
questions.D: Government
questions.explanation: Mr Ayesoro was the Government teacher whose facial marks frightened Bibi.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the students' derogatory nickname for Mr Ayesoro was
questions.A: Mr Owala
questions.B: Principo
questions.C: King Oloja
questions.D: Englisher
questions.explanation: 'Owala' (or 'Wala') is a mocking Yoruba term for someone with prominent facial marks.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, after Mrs Ladele's complaint, Mr Ayesoro was transferred to
questions.A: Beesway Group of School on the outskirts of Lagos
questions.B: the school's boarding house as a live-in house master
questions.C: Stardom Hub, the property-management arm of the company
questions.D: Stardom Kiddies, the primary arm of the school
questions.explanation: Rather than educate the pupils about culture, management hid the teacher in its property-management wing.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the treatment of Mr Ayesoro chiefly illustrates
questions.A: the cruelty of students towards teachers from rural areas
questions.B: the need for stricter discipline in elite private schools
questions.C: the danger of allowing teachers with tribal marks near children
questions.D: how schools put fee-paying parents above the dignity of teachers
questions.explanation: A qualified teacher lost his classroom simply to keep three children's fees, showing the commodification of education.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, in the chapter 'Snake in the Roof', the MD is alarmed to discover
questions.A: about seventeen staff cars parked on school land
questions.B: a live snake in the school's roof
questions.C: that the accountant had stolen money
questions.D: that teachers were planning a strike
questions.explanation: Inspecting land near the back gate, Mrs Gloss finds a hidden car park full of vehicles with Stardom stickers.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the staff had been able to buy their cars through
questions.A: loans from the Stardom Cooperative Society
questions.B: gifts from wealthy parents at Open Day
questions.C: car loans from a commercial bank in Lekki
questions.D: salary advances approved by the MD
questions.explanation: The accountant explains that the cooperative gave the loans, with repayments deducted from salaries.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the expression 'hanging a snake in the roof and going to bed' is used by
questions.A: Chief Mrs Solape Bayo
questions.B: Mrs Ibidun Gloss
questions.C: Mr Jeremi Amos
questions.D: Mr Audu
questions.explanation: The board chairman, Chief Mrs Solape Bayo, uses the image at the emergency board meeting.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, 'hanging a snake in the roof and going to bed' means
questions.A: sleeping peacefully after a hard day's work
questions.B: keeping dangerous pets inside the house
questions.C: ignoring a danger that could strike at any moment
questions.D: building a house cheaply with poor materials
questions.explanation: The board sees the rich cooperative as a threat the school is foolishly living with.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the board's real fear about the cooperative was that the staff might
questions.A: use the money to start a rival school
questions.B: resign in large numbers at once
questions.C: buy even more expensive cars
questions.D: sue the school over their salaries
questions.explanation: Chief Mrs Bayo worries that financially independent teachers could set up a competing school.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, in response to the cooperative's wealth, the board decided to
questions.A: close the cooperative society down with immediate effect
questions.B: reward the accountant for managing the funds so well
questions.C: increase all salaries so that staff need no more loans
questions.D: cap staff loans at N250,000 and require the MD's approval
questions.explanation: The board also demanded oversight of the cooperative's elections and activities.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the fact that the teachers hid their cars in a distant car park suggests that they
questions.A: expected management to react badly to any sign of their prosperity
questions.B: were ashamed of buying second-hand cars with borrowed money
questions.C: had no parking permits for the main car park by the gate
questions.D: were planning to sell the cars to raise money to travel
questions.explanation: Their fear proves justified when the board moves to cripple the cooperative.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, on Open Day, Mr Guta complains about the sentence
questions.A: 'Ade as well as Jide come early'
questions.B: 'Ade and Jide comes early'
questions.C: 'Ade as well as Jide comes early'
questions.D: 'Ade or Jide come early'
questions.explanation: Mr Guta wrongly believes the verb should be 'come'; the MD orders Mr Fafore's sack on the strength of the complaint.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo defends Mr Fafore by explaining that
questions.A: an English teacher of twenty-two years cannot possibly make such an error
questions.B: the MD had no power to sack a teacher without the board's approval
questions.C: the parent had no right to read a private note written to his son
questions.D: with 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first noun, so 'comes' is correct
questions.explanation: Phrases like 'as well as' and 'together with' do not make the subject plural; a smartphone check proves Bepo right.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Mr Fafore teaches
questions.A: English
questions.B: Mathematics
questions.C: Government
questions.D: Physics
questions.explanation: Mr Fafore is the senior English teacher whose correct sentence nearly cost him his job.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, which detail shows Mr Fafore's dedication despite his poor pay?
questions.A: He bought a car through the cooperative so as never to be late
questions.B: He teaches free extra lessons every Saturday in the school hall
questions.C: He rises at 4 a.m. daily to reach school by 6 a.m. and sleep on his desk
questions.D: He lives in the school boarding house as an unpaid house master
questions.explanation: Fafore sleeps on his desk after arriving at dawn from distant Ogun State to avoid Lagos traffic.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Mr Fafore lives far away in Ogun State because
questions.A: he was born and raised there and inherited his father's house
questions.B: his wife runs a shop there and refused to move to Lagos
questions.C: the school posted him to supervise its new branch there
questions.D: he cannot afford rent in the Lekki area on N175,000 a month
questions.explanation: Twenty-two years after graduating he earns 175,000 naira and cannot even afford his own school's fees for his children.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, after the MD realises her mistake, the tension is broken when
questions.A: Mr Audu bows and jokingly asks for his own sack letter
questions.B: Mr Guta apologises to the whole staff for his ignorance
questions.C: Mr Fafore resigns in protest and walks out of the hall
questions.D: Bepo walks out of the meeting in silent disgust
questions.explanation: Audu's dramatic Japanese bow and demand to be sacked like the 'great teacher' Fafore makes everyone laugh.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo's memory of Iya Mathew pouring cassava powder on his head shows that he
questions.A: was once a farmer who grew cassava
questions.B: was a difficult and stubborn tenant
questions.C: has personally known poverty and humiliation
questions.D: dislikes landladies to this day
questions.explanation: The landlady humiliated him over 2,500 naira electricity money; the memory explains why he hates issuing sack letters.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the teachers describe Stardom as a 'one-man business' to complain that
questions.A: the school has only one owner and no board of directors
questions.B: the school is too small to be called a group of schools
questions.C: the salaries are paid late whenever the owner travels
questions.D: their jobs depend on the employer's mood rather than on rules
questions.explanation: Mr Audu and Mr Obi lament the lack of job security in private schools.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo pointed out to Mr Egi Meko that the name 'Beesway Group of School' should be
questions.A: 'Beesway Group of Schools'
questions.B: 'Beesway School'
questions.C: 'Beesway Groups of School'
questions.D: 'Beesway Schools Group'
questions.explanation: 'Group of' must be followed by a plural noun; the director refused to accept the correction.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Mr Meko refused to correct the school's name, claiming that it was
questions.A: registered abroad
questions.B: his late father's idea
questions.C: divinely inspired
questions.D: too costly to change
questions.explanation: Meko also cited the Corporate Affairs Commission registration and mocked Bepo as an 'Englisher'.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo finally left Beesway after
questions.A: being denied a promotion he had been promised for two years
questions.B: the school was shut down by the state government inspectors
questions.C: losing a court case over the school's grammatically wrong name
questions.D: seeing the director and other men burying a live cow at night
questions.explanation: At about 2:30 a.m. Bepo saw five men leading a cow to a grave-sized pit on the school premises.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo confronted the men at Beesway armed with
questions.A: a machete and his crucifix
questions.B: a licensed pistol
questions.C: a torch and a whistle
questions.D: a wooden club
questions.explanation: He went down with a machete and crucifix, but a man struck his wrist with a club and disarmed him.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the next morning Mr Meko explained the night ritual as
questions.A: a special prayer for his late father
questions.B: a farming exercise
questions.C: a students' science project
questions.D: a police operation
questions.explanation: Meko apologised for the assault and claimed nothing occultic happened; Bepo left within two hours.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo decided not to report the Beesway incident to the police because
questions.A: he had no witnesses and the pit had been filled in by morning
questions.B: the director had threatened to harm his wife and daughters
questions.C: he could not afford a long legal fight against a rich man in a corrupt system
questions.D: Mrs Gloss advised him to forget the matter and join Stardom
questions.explanation: He reflects that he would even be asked to pay for the police's paper and fuel.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, at Fruitful Future, Mr Ogo offered to
questions.A: buy the school outright and keep Bepo on as its headmaster
questions.B: enrol his ten children if the fees were halved for him
questions.C: donate a library and a bus in exchange for free tuition
questions.D: sprinkle grains of corn around the school as a ritual to attract pupils
questions.explanation: For 35,000 naira Ogo promised a ritual that would 'flood the school with pupils'; Bepo refused.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, years later, Mr Ogo was
questions.A: arrested for killing a woman in a fake fertility ritual
questions.B: elected chairman of the local government council
questions.C: installed as a traditional chief in his home town
questions.D: employed as a security guard at Stardom Schools
questions.explanation: Bepo saw him on the news, arrested for dropping a woman into a grave-sized pit.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the recurring image of the 'grave-sized pit' in the novel symbolises
questions.A: the school's endless and costly building projects
questions.B: Bepo's secret fear of dying and being buried abroad
questions.C: the predatory nature of rituals used to chase wealth
questions.D: the poor state of the roads leading to the school
questions.explanation: The pit is where the cow is buried at Beesway and where Ogo's victim dies, linking both crimes to greed.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo believes a school grows through
questions.A: rituals and special prayers conducted by powerful prophets
questions.B: political connections and friends in the ministry
questions.C: cheap fees, free uniforms and generous scholarships
questions.D: good teacher welfare, sound curriculum and strong parent relations
questions.explanation: Rejecting Ogo's ritual, Bepo insists genuine growth comes from professional practices, not supernatural shortcuts.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the feud between Banky and Tosh began with
questions.A: a Best Dancer competition which Tosh won 3-2
questions.B: a football match which Banky's team lost
questions.C: an inter-house debate which Tosh won
questions.D: a quarrel over a bed space in the hostel
questions.explanation: Banky's mother protested the dance result, and the mothers later clashed at the PTA elections.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, during Speech Day, Banky's offensive remark to the audience was
questions.A: 'Tosh cannot speak good English, so how can he lead you?'
questions.B: 'Tosh still owes school fees, so he cannot be your prefect'
questions.C: 'Instead of voting for the son of an ex-convict, cast your vote for me'
questions.D: 'Tosh failed his examinations and should not be in SSS 2'
questions.explanation: The attack on Tosh's father caused chaos in the hall and a lawsuit between the two families.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Tosh's father, Chief Didi Ogba, is
questions.A: a school proprietor who once owned Beesway Group of School
questions.B: the school's accountant and head of the cooperative
questions.C: an immigration officer at the Ikoyi passport office
questions.D: a top lawyer and politician who spent 36 months in detention
questions.explanation: Chief Ogba was tried over a N2.5 billion contract; his company was ordered to refund the money but he was not found directly guilty.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, one condition for contesting the prefect elections at Stardom is that a candidate must
questions.A: owe no school fees
questions.B: be a boarder
questions.C: be in SSS 3
questions.D: speak a Nigerian language
questions.explanation: Aspirants must be academically sound, morally upright and debt-free, besides buying an intent form.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the MD's remark 'ask a tenant to lead the landlord' is used to justify
questions.A: sacking teachers who borrow heavily from the cooperative
questions.B: raising the boarding fees for students from poorer homes
questions.C: barring students who owe fees from contesting elections
questions.D: the policy of one local excursion for every class each term
questions.explanation: 'If you want a debtor to lead fee payers, ask a tenant to lead the landlord' defends the debt-free rule.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the prefect election arrangement is a satire of Nigerian politics because
questions.A: students cannot vote, since teachers choose the prefects in a secret ballot
questions.B: teachers contest as well and always defeat the student candidates
questions.C: the MD chooses the winners herself and merely announces them to the school
questions.D: money decides who can contest, and parents' party rivalries poison the process
questions.explanation: Forms cost up to N50,000 and the boys' fathers belong to rival parties, mirroring adult politics.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the Invention Club's 'Breath Project' aims to
questions.A: build a phone from recycled panels and chips
questions.B: plant a thousand trees round the school
questions.C: produce cheap oxygen for village hospitals
questions.D: compose and record a new school anthem
questions.explanation: The five-year project attracted media attention and funding from the NGO Life Grid.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo's involvement with the Invention Club shows that he
questions.A: was originally a science teacher
questions.B: wanted to leave teaching for technology
questions.C: believes invention is not limited by one's discipline
questions.D: disliked the arts
questions.explanation: Though an English teacher, Bepo is the club's patron and vows to return for the phone's launch.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo's excursion policy at Stardom provided
questions.A: one international trip every term for the senior classes
questions.B: excursions for SSS 3 students only, in their final term
questions.C: two visits to Badagry every year for every class in the school
questions.D: one local excursion each term and one international trip a year
questions.explanation: The policy exposed pupils to Nigeria's natural, historical and cultural sites before many left to study abroad.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo insisted on excursions because he wanted pupils who might later study abroad to
questions.A: know their fatherland well before leaving it
questions.B: learn how to travel alone without their parents
questions.C: avoid boredom during the long school terms
questions.D: pass their Geography and History examinations
questions.explanation: He feared elite children would leave Nigeria without ever knowing it.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the waterfall described as the highest in West Africa is
questions.A: Erin Ijesha Waterfalls
questions.B: Gurara Falls
questions.C: Owu Waterfalls
questions.D: Ikogosi Warm Springs
questions.explanation: Owu Waterfalls in Kwara State is presented as the highest in West Africa.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Ikogosi in Ekiti State is remembered in the novel as
questions.A: the site of the first storey building
questions.B: the home of the Ooni
questions.C: a warm spring discovered by Rev. John S. McGee in 1852
questions.D: the venue of the Osun festival
questions.explanation: The novel recounts the folklore and history behind each site the pupils visited.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo took pupils to Ajegunle to teach them that
questions.A: slums are dangerous places that must be avoided at night
questions.B: Lagos is overpopulated because of migration from villages
questions.C: footballers from poor homes always become rich and famous
questions.D: being born in a slum does not condemn one to poverty
questions.explanation: He cited Odion Ighalo and Victor Osimhen, who rose from the low ends of Lagos to stardom.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo's phrase 'life is a potpourri of opposites' is illustrated by
questions.A: contrasting visits to Banana Island and to slums like Ajegunle
questions.B: the novelty football match between the staff and the students
questions.C: the arts-versus-sciences debate at Bepo's farewell ceremony
questions.D: the reduction of boarding fees alongside the higher excursion fee
questions.explanation: Pupils saw affluent estates and corporate offices alongside slums and charity homes.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, at the Black Heritage Museum in Badagry, Bepo compares the slave trade to
questions.A: the boarding-house system in elite schools
questions.B: the payment of school fees by poor parents
questions.C: the modern rush of Nigerians to migrate abroad
questions.D: the prefect elections at Stardom Schools
questions.explanation: He sees japa as a voluntary 'new slavery' in which Africans again leave to build foreign economies.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the First Storey Building in Badagry is significant in the novel as the place where
questions.A: Bepo was born and spent his childhood
questions.B: the Bible was translated into Yoruba
questions.C: the captured slaves were sold at auction
questions.D: the Akran of Badagry was first crowned
questions.explanation: The pupils visit the Akran's palace, the First Storey Building and the Point of No Return.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo had allowed his passport to expire for two years because
questions.A: he had never been keen on relocating
questions.B: it had been stolen
questions.C: he could not afford the renewal fee
questions.D: he had been banned from travelling
questions.explanation: Only his family's pressure turned the renewal into an emergency.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo chose to renew his passport in Ibadan in order to
questions.A: visit his home town and see his aged mother before travelling
questions.B: avoid the crowds and hassles at the Lagos passport offices
questions.C: meet Tai, an old school friend who worked at the passport office
questions.D: attend a conference of principals holding in the city
questions.explanation: The japa wave had created maddening crowds at the Ikoyi and Ikeja offices.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Tai, the agent, charged Bepo N100,000 although the official fee was
questions.explanation: Bepo pays a 30,000-naira premium to the agent, who turns out to be a business-centre operator in a syndicate.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the journey from Lagos to Ibadan took only about 50 minutes because
questions.A: Bepo travelled by the new train service
questions.B: the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway had been reconstructed
questions.C: he travelled at night when the road was free
questions.D: he rode on a motorcycle through the traffic
questions.explanation: A decade earlier the same trip in a school bus had taken two hours.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the many religious camps along the expressway make Bepo wonder whether Nigeria has
questions.A: 'too many roads and too few cars'
questions.B: 'many religionists but few godly people'
questions.C: 'no honest pastors'
questions.D: 'too few schools'
questions.explanation: The thought fits his own situation: he is bribing an agent even as he passes the camps.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo's passport renewal is finally delayed by
questions.A: the sudden arrest of Tai by immigration officers
questions.B: a network glitch during the validation of his NIN
questions.C: a public holiday declared by the federal government
questions.D: a missing birth certificate and tax clearance
questions.explanation: After paying the syndicate he is defeated by technology: the NIN office cannot validate him for three weeks.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the brown roofs of Ibadan remind Bepo of
questions.A: Achebe's Things Fall Apart
questions.B: J. P. Clark's poem 'Ibadan'
questions.C: Soyinka's Ake
questions.D: the Third Mainland Bridge
questions.explanation: He also recalls Adelakun's Under the Brown Rusted Roofs and Ibadan's first university and television station.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo's experience at the passport office shows that
questions.A: digitisation had finally ended corruption in the passport process
questions.B: officials sabotage the online system to keep an extortion racket alive
questions.C: the agents are in fact senior immigration officers in disguise
questions.D: the Ibadan office is far worse than those in Ikoyi and Ikeja
questions.explanation: Government claims the process is fully digital, yet the erratic portal drives applicants to pay agents like Tai.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo changed his departure date and paid an airline penalty because
questions.A: his visa was delayed at the British High Commission
questions.B: the school wanted time for a befitting send-off
questions.C: his wife asked him to wait for the girls' school holidays
questions.D: the airline cancelled the flight at the last minute
questions.explanation: The school gladly covered the 100-dollar penalty so that the farewell could hold.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, in the farewell debate, the winning side argued that
questions.A: the sciences have contributed more to Nigeria's development
questions.B: the arts have contributed more to Nigeria's development
questions.C: migration is good for Nigeria
questions.D: boarding schools are better than day schools
questions.explanation: SSS 3, citing Nollywood and Soyinka's Nobel Prize, won the debate in Bepo's honour.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the banner at Bepo's farewell read
questions.A: 'Goodbye and God Bless, Principo'
questions.B: 'For He Gave Stardom His Very Best'
questions.C: 'Point of No Return: Farewell, Sir'
questions.D: 'The Lekki Headmaster Goes to London'
questions.explanation: The banner in the main hall summed up 24 years of service.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the dance that sends Bepo into a hallucination of the slave trade is
questions.A: the Bata dance of the Yoruba
questions.B: the Atilogwu dance of the Igbo
questions.C: the Koroso dance of the Hausa
questions.D: the Canoe dance of the Badagry people
questions.explanation: The canoe dance takes him back to the slavery museum; he recovers only when the performance ends.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo was employed at Stardom twenty-four years earlier by
questions.A: Mrs Ibidun Gloss
questions.B: Chief David Aje, the founder
questions.C: Chief Mrs Solape Bayo
questions.D: Mr Ope Wande
questions.explanation: The MD's late father interviewed Bepo himself and called him an 'essential teacher'.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the MD refuses to announce the amount of Bepo's farewell cheque because
questions.A: the sum was embarrassingly small
questions.B: it might tempt other staff to 'run away' too
questions.C: the board had forbidden it
questions.D: Bepo asked her not to
questions.explanation: She reveals only that it is a domiciliary cheque in foreign currency.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the Yoruba proverb about the master carver whose works live on expresses the theme of
questions.A: migration
questions.B: legacy
questions.C: corruption
questions.D: poverty
questions.explanation: Bepo reflects that even after he leaves, the minds he has shaped will endure.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, at the end of the farewell, Bepo
questions.A: delivers a long and witty speech of thanks to the staff
questions.B: breaks down in tears at the podium, unable to speak
questions.C: announces to the shocked hall that he will not travel
questions.D: hands over the school keys to the new principal
questions.explanation: His tears mirror the breakdown in the opening chapter; the whole hall weeps with him.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the MD jokingly calls Britain
questions.A: 'the land of no return'
questions.B: 'the heaven and haven of good things'
questions.C: 'a cold and hungry island'
questions.D: 'the home of grammar'
questions.explanation: Her tribute laments that Stardom and Nigeria are losing Bepo to Britain.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo leaves home at 3 p.m. for a 10 p.m. flight because
questions.A: he had once missed a flight because of Lagos traffic
questions.B: the airline demanded early check-in
questions.C: he wanted to shop at the airport
questions.D: the school bus was leaving early
questions.explanation: He is determined not to repeat the day he missed a British Airways flight.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, before leaving, Bepo sold his SUV to
questions.A: Mr Audu
questions.B: the school accountant
questions.C: his landlord, Mr Ogunwale
questions.D: Tai, the agent
questions.explanation: He sold the Pathfinder to the accountant and gave his freezer and electronics to his landlady.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Jide, the landlord's grandson, was coached by Bepo at weekends in
questions.A: Mathematics and Physics
questions.B: elocution and African history
questions.C: football and athletics
questions.D: Yoruba and Hausa
questions.explanation: Bepo feels guilty about abandoning the boy's weekend lessons.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo is disturbed when seven-year-old Kemi uses the word
questions.A: 'Principo'
questions.B: 'japa'
questions.C: 'ritual'
questions.D: 'visa'
questions.explanation: That so young a child knows 'japa' shows how deeply the urge to flee has entered Nigerian life.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, in his nightmare at the airport, Bepo
questions.A: sees Stardom Schools burning to the ground in his absence
questions.B: is ordered by a white slave master to board a slave ship
questions.C: loses his passport and ticket minutes before boarding
questions.D: is arrested by immigration officers for using an agent
questions.explanation: He wakes screaming 'no' just as an airline official taps him to announce boarding.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo's airport nightmare suggests that he sees migration as
questions.A: a well-earned holiday
questions.B: a new form of slavery
questions.C: a professional promotion
questions.D: a religious duty
questions.explanation: The dream links his flight to London with the slave ships that left Badagry.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, on the Monday after his departure, the gloomy assembly is interrupted by
questions.A: the arrival of a new principal
questions.B: a shout of 'Principoo' as Bepo reappears
questions.C: a fire alarm
questions.D: the MD's resignation
questions.explanation: The pupils sweep Bepo off his feet in a frenzied celebration.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo's final declaration on his return is
questions.A: 'I will come back next year when my papers are ready'
questions.B: 'I am back! My heart is here! I am here to complete my mission!'
questions.C: 'London is now my home, but Stardom is in my heart'
questions.D: 'Goodbye, Stardom, for ever; I have done my very best'
questions.explanation: His return, celebrated with the school's victory song, ends the novel on a note of hope.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo's decision to return to Stardom is best described as
questions.A: cowardice in the face of the challenge of a new life abroad
questions.B: the triumph of personal conviction over family and social pressure
questions.C: blind obedience to the wishes of the Managing Director
questions.D: a calculated wish for an even bigger farewell cheque
questions.explanation: Despite a UK job and his wife's ultimatum, he chooses his mission with Nigerian youth.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, which of the following is NOT a major theme of the novel?
questions.A: migration and identity
questions.B: leadership and sacrifice
questions.C: space exploration
questions.D: corruption in public institutions
questions.explanation: The novel deals with japa, leadership, education, corruption and cultural heritage, not space exploration.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Mrs Ibidun Gloss is best described as
questions.A: a careless and lazy administrator who leaves everything to Bepo
questions.B: a pragmatic businesswoman who guards the school's image and finances
questions.C: a timid woman who is ruled by her board and her senior staff
questions.D: a classroom teacher promoted beyond her ability and experience
questions.explanation: She inherited the school from her father, holds a law degree and puts business first, yet respects Bepo.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the secret physical pain that Mrs Gloss endures is used to show that
questions.A: she should hand over the school to a younger person
questions.B: wealth and power do not protect one from vulnerability
questions.C: the school clinic is too poorly equipped to treat her
questions.D: she is too old and too sick to lead a modern school
questions.explanation: Her chronic pain mirrors her hidden fear that her staff might grow strong enough to challenge her.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Mr Audu functions in the novel chiefly as
questions.A: the villain
questions.B: a source of comic relief
questions.C: Bepo's rival
questions.D: the voice of the parents
questions.explanation: From coining the nickname to his Japanese bow, Audu's jokes lighten the tensest scenes.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo's attitude to migration throughout the novel is one of
questions.A: eager and open enthusiasm
questions.B: reluctance rooted in patriotism
questions.C: total indifference to it
questions.D: fear of flying long distances
questions.explanation: He believes it makes no sense to abandon a developing nation to help build a developed one.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, the novel presents private education in Nigeria mainly as
questions.A: a charitable service run by dedicated and selfless people
questions.B: a heavily monetised business where fees outweigh principle
questions.C: a responsibility that government has wrongly abandoned
questions.D: a failing system in which no competent teacher remains
questions.explanation: Fee manipulation, the Ayesoro and Fafore affairs and the costly prefect forms all show schooling as commerce.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: In The Lekki Headmaster, Bepo can be described as a round character because he
questions.A: appears in every single chapter of the novel from start to finish
questions.B: combines humour, empathy and firmness with private fear and doubt
questions.C: never once changes his mind about anything in the story
questions.D: is the narrator through whose eyes every event is seen
questions.explanation: The novel shows both his public confidence and his private tears, and his views develop to a final decision.
